name: TPR total: exporter (Teleport API) vs Prometheus gauge
why: Two independent measurements of the same quantity. The exporter asks the Teleport API directly; teleport_connected_resources is emitted by auth from heartbeat state. They should agree, and when they do not, one of them is wrong in a way no single-source check can see. This replaced a comparison against the usage tracker's tpr_history table, which had recorded 720 consecutive zeros because the tracker's identity expired and it swallowed every fetch error. The tracker was retired on 2026-09-01 and the exporter replaces it.

name: TPR total: exporter vs Access Graph inventory
why: A third independent view of the same quantity. The exporter lists resources through the Teleport API; the Access Graph builds its own inventory from a separate ingestion path. They derive the number differently, so agreement is meaningful and divergence usually means the Access Graph has gone stale. Enterprise-only, so this skips cleanly on OSS.

b.label: Access Graph resource nodes
b.query: SET search_path TO ${tenant}; SELECT count(*) FROM nodes WHERE kind='resource'

name: Exporter collectors are all reporting
why: A collector that stops is supposed to WITHDRAW its metrics, so absence is the correct signal rather than a zero. That makes it invisible to any check that only looks at values. collector_up is the explicit health signal; this asserts every collector is up. The old tracker's month of silent zeros is exactly what this catches on the first scrape rather than the first quarterly review.

name: Freshness: the exporter is still collecting
why: A collector that hangs rather than errors keeps its last value on the dashboard indefinitely, which reads as a current measurement. Compares the age of the newest successful collection against a threshold. Collectors run on a 5 minute cadence, so 15 minutes is three missed cycles.

b.label: age of the newest successful collection (seconds)

name: Teleport API version matches the exporter build
why: New resource kinds land in MINOR Teleport releases, so a binary built against an older minor under-counts a newer cluster and publishes the shortfall as fact. The exporter detects this at startup and sets the metric; this surfaces it as a validation failure rather than leaving it in a log line nobody reads.

name: MWI bots: exporter vs distinct bots seen joining
why: The exporter lists bots from the API; the audit log records bot.join events. These measure related but not identical things -- a configured bot that never joins appears in one and not the other -- so the tolerance is loose. It is here to catch a collector reading zero, not to police an off-by-one.

b.label: distinct bots seen joining in 30d
b.query: SELECT count(DISTINCT event_data->>'bot_name') FROM public.events WHERE event_type='bot.join' AND event_time > now() - interval '30 days'
